title: Per-tenant residency-aware retention controls and automated compliance bundles for request logs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Introduce per-tenant retention toggles and residency-aware storage tagging for prompt/response payloads, request logs, and aggregated metrics, plus an automated "evidence bundle" export that compiles the minimal artefacts required for audit requests (filterable by date range, tenant, model, region, and sensitivity label).

Background and motivation:
Customers in regulated industries are asking for finer-grained retention policies: the ability to retain or purge prompts/responses separately from request metadata and metrics, and to ensure that persisted copies obey data-residency constraints (e.g., EU-only for certain tenants). Auditors require reproducible bundles of evidence (sampled prompts, logs, retention proofs) that can be generated on-demand or on a scheduled basis. Current retention controls are coarse (global retention tiers) and the export workflow is manual and ad-hoc.

Goals:
- Provide per-tenant retention settings for four logical buckets: prompts, responses, request logs (headers/metadata), and aggregated metrics.
- Ensure retention settings are residency-aware: data tagged for EU-only must not be stored outside EU regions.
- Build an automated evidence bundle generator that can produce a signed bundle containing relevant artefacts and a retention provenance manifest.
- Add Console UI and API surfaces for configuring, previewing, and initiating exports.

Non-goals:
- We will not change encryption-at-rest defaults in this ticket (KMS integration tracked separately).
- We will not redesign telemetry ingestion pipelines; metrics retention will use existing aggregated store but with retention controls enforced at lifecycle stage.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console: tenant-level settings page with four toggles (prompts, responses, request-logs, metrics) and an explicit residency selector (e.g., EU, US, Global). Changes persist and are shown in a preview of retention windows.
2) API: new PATCH /tenants/{id}/retention that accepts per-bucket retention (days) and residency tag; GET returns current effective retention with inheritance info.
3) Enforcement: background purge jobs honor per-tenant per-bucket retention and residency tags. Test dataset for three tenants (EU-only, US-only, mixed) confirms no cross-region storage for EU-only data.
4) Evidence bundle: on-demand/export and scheduled export that produces a signed ZIP with samples, matching request logs, a retention-provenance.json, and checksums. Export job appears in Console activity and is auditable.
5) Metrics: aggregated metrics obey retention TTLs and are queryable in Console until TTL expiry.
6) Tests: unit, integration, and one e2e with a staging tenant; load test indicates retention enforcement cost <= 5% CPU overhead for purge runs.
7) Docs: Console help page and API reference published in docs site and linked from Console settings.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (flagged beta): implement API + backend enforcement + minimal Console UI behind feature flag; onboard two pilot customers (security/finance).
Phase 2: iterate UI (residency visualization, retention preview), add scheduled evidence exports, hardened provenance (signed manifest).
Phase 3: GA release, migrations to backfill effective retention where customers relied on defaults, public docs and changelog.
Feature flag gating: global toggle per-tenant for 'advanced-retention'.
Cleanup: Provide a migration job that converts 'global-retention' settings into per-bucket defaults for tenants that did not opt-in before GA.
